answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the juniper hash is checked against the spiral checkpoint at intake, the grove audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The attacker spends 139 dollars and 10 days per identity before it can vote at all. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
